words.gloss: even to the size of a millet seed
even to the size of a palmyra tree

literal: Even to the size of a millet seed, not sulking is necessary, when love, even to the size of a palmyra tree, comes abundantly.
translation: One must avoid feigned anger even to the tiny measure of a millet seed, when love arises in abundance, swelling to the vast size of a palmyra tree.
modern: பனைமரம் போன்ற பெரிய அளவில் காம உணர்வு நிறைந்து வரும்போது, தினை அளவு கூட ஊடல் கொள்ளாமல் இருக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet describes the urgency of lovers who are eager to reunite. The speaker explains that when love and desire swell to a massive size, symbolized by the tall palmyra tree, one must not indulge in even the tiniest bit of feigned anger, symbolized by the tiny millet seed. Any delay caused by sulking, however brief or small, becomes unbearable when passion is overwhelming. The contrast between the tiny millet seed and the large palmyra tree beautifully illustrates the disproportionate pain that even a minor lovers' tiff can cause when desire is at its peak.
